clue.text: Ridiculous — content's back to front, it's clear !

indicators.note: the run taken from inside is then read in the opposite direction, last letter first
the contents of a word are the letters held inside it, here a run from the middle of Ridiculous

explanation.surface: An exclamation that something is plainly absurd, with its contents jumbled the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content's' takes DICUL from inside riDICULous; 'back to front' turns it round. The definition is really 'clear', with 'it's' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucid explanation is transparent and easy to follow.

clue.text: Foil him by talking through your hat

definitions.text: Foil him by talking through your hat

parts.words: Foil him by talking through your hat
parts.note: literally, speaking from behind a hat hides your mouth from someone who follows speech by watching it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Talking through your hat' usually means talking nonsense; here it means literally hiding your mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who understands speech by watching the movements of a speaker's mouth.

clue.text: Sound the Gordons, say, over their leader

parts.note: the Gordons are a Scottish clan
the first letter of Gordons

explanation.surface: A call to sound the bugle for the Gordon Highlanders above their commander.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts CLAN above G.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud ringing metallic noise.

clue.text: Freed from fear, might you say-being dead?

indicators.note: signals that the word is judged by how it is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: funk is old slang for fear, so de-funked would mean rid of it

explanation.surface: A musing on whether release from all fear is the same as death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funk' (a state of panic) is old British slang for fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Something no longer living or in operation is extinct.

clue.text: One giving a name to a film

definitions.meaning: a sponsor at a christening who presents the child for naming

explanation.definitionFit: A male sponsor at baptism, and the title of Coppola's famous gangster movie.

clue.text: Has rig that's uncommonly flashy

indicators.note: used in an unusual way, so the letters are set out differently

explanation.surface: Someone owns an outfit that is unusually showy.
explanation.definitionFit: Garish colours are loud and tasteless, much like gaudy ones.

clue.text: Find close of play recorded

parts.note: something recorded is on disc
when play is finished it is over

explanation.surface: An instruction to track down the end of a match captured on record.
explanation.definitionFit: To find something is to come upon it or uncover it.

clue.text: A race united without it is in harmony

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

indicators.note: here means lacking, so the letters of one word are removed from the other

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A race of united people is in harmony without something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes IT from UNITED, leaving UNED.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuned to the same pitch, so in accord or agreement.

clue.text: Plant show where Herbert has a drink about one

parts.note: Herb is a short form of the name Herbert

indicators.note: one piece goes round another, the drink placed about the numeral

parts.note: rum is a drink
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: At a flower show, a man named Herbert has a drink around one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts RUM round I to give RIUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A collection of dried, preserved specimens laid out for study and display.

clue.text: What Poe's time does with a runic one

definitions.text: What Poe's time does with a runic one

parts.words: What Poe's time does with a runic one
parts.note: Poe's poem The Bells pairs 'keeping time, time, time' with 'a sort of Runic' verse, the two words matching in sound

explanation.surface: A question about what the timing in a Poe poem does with an ancient one.
explanation.definitionFit: Words that share an ending sound, as time does with its partner in Poe's line.

clue.text: Do they provide the sole support of speakers?

definitions.text: Do they provide the sole support of speakers?

parts.words: Do they provide the sole support of speakers?
parts.note: raised stages hold up orators, while thick-soled shoes of the same name support the soles of anyone wearing them

explanation.surface: A question about what alone holds up public orators.
explanation.definitionFit: Raised stages for speakers, and also shoes with very thick soles.

clue.text: Linger like J. C. Harris's baby

definitions.meaning: Joel Chandler Harris wrote the Uncle Remus tale of the Tar-Baby, a doll made of tar

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently: one rhymes with 'marry', the other with 'starry'.
explanation.definitionFit: To dawdle or stay; also resembling or covered in tar, like the sticky Tar-Baby of the Uncle Remus stories.

clue.text: Sporting event could end in a big scramble

definitions.text: Sporting event could end in a big scramble

parts.words: Sporting event could end in a big scramble
parts.note: a children's race where each runner balances a fragile object on cutlery, and dropping it may leave it scrambled

explanation.walkthrough: This race is a fixture of British school sports days.
explanation.definitionFit: A school sports-day race in which runners carry a breakable item balanced on a utensil.

clue.text: In which a society girl discussed a meal?

definitions.text: In which a society girl discussed a meal?

parts.words: In which a society girl discussed a meal?
parts.note: split into parts, a debutante (society girl) and a past tense of eating, describing a formal discussion

explanation.surface: A question about where a young socialite talked over her dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as DEB (debutante, a society girl) plus ATE (had a meal); the whole is a formal discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal discussion of a motion, as in a debating society.

clue.text: Beauty grabs a gun in this musical piece

indicators.note: a thing that grabs another holds it inside

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman
gat is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A beautiful woman seizes a weapon during a musical performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beauty' looks like part of the scene but supplies the outer letters; 'grabs' is the container signal, and 'gat' is old American slang for a pistol.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, light composition, often for piano.

clue.text: Uninterrupted bore as it would be to north-bound traffic

definitions.text: Uninterrupted bore as it would be to north-bound traffic

parts.words: Uninterrupted bore as it would be to north-bound traffic
parts.note: a north wind blows straight into the faces of travellers going north, a steady blast against them

explanation.surface: A tedious unbroken stretch faced by drivers heading north.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind blowing directly against the direction of travel, like a northerly for those going north.

clue.text: A poor cyclist wanted to give her a ring

definitions.text: A poor cyclist wanted to give her a ring

parts.words: A poor cyclist wanted to give her a ring
parts.note: the old song's singer cannot afford a carriage and offers a bicycle built for two while proposing marriage

explanation.walkthrough: A 'ring' is both an engagement ring and the sound of the bell in the song's title.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1892 music-hall song about a 'bicycle built for two', whose singer wants to marry the girl.

clue.text: Ponder how to take care of it in a football crowd

parts.note: c/o is the abbreviation for care of on letters

indicators.note: one piece sits within another, the word placed inside the crowd

parts.note: a gate is the attendance at a football match
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question of how one might look after something amid a football crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take care of' looks like the verb but supplies the postal abbreviation; 'gate' is British for the size of the crowd at a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To ponder is to think deeply and at length.

clue.text: Latvia's capital party-on with the dance !

parts.note: Riga is the capital city of Latvia
a do is a party
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone in Riga calls for the party to carry on with the dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively old dance in duple time, originally from Provence.

clue.text: Furniture not employed for nudist shows

definitions.meaning: a sideboard or chest of drawers
a theatre helper who puts costumes on actors has no work where nobody is clothed

explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen sideboard with shelves, and a backstage helper who clothes actors.

clue.text: Pitch tent in an island retreat, of course

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other, the tent pitched inside the island
to retreat is to go backwards, so the island's abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: to camp is to pitch a tent

explanation.surface: Naturally, one would set up a tent on a remote island hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' sends the island abbreviation backwards before the tent goes in. 'of course' reads as 'naturally' but means a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaded prawns served as a dish, one course of a restaurant meal.

clue.text: Chip bar

definitions.meaning: a token used in games or for gambling
a shop or pub surface over which goods are served

explanation.definitionFit: A gaming token, and the flat-topped serving surface in a shop or bar.

clue.text: 'e's brought in an Olympic prize of long ago

indicators.note: one thing brought into another is placed inside it

parts.note: a gold medal is the top Olympic prize
the clue presents the letter E with an apostrophe, giving E

explanation.surface: A Cockney man is awarded an Olympic medal from the distant past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in' puts E inside A GOLD; ''e' reads as Cockney 'he' but is just the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient things have existed for a very long time.

clue.text: When fast time's cut in half, mum's the word

definitions.text: When fast time's cut in half, mum's the word

parts.words: When fast time's cut in half, mum's the word
parts.note: the fourth Sunday of Lent falls halfway through the fasting season and is the day for honouring mothers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum's the word' looks like a call for silence, but here mums are literally the point of the day; it is the British Mother's Day, in mid-Lent.
explanation.definitionFit: The UK's Mother's Day, held on the fourth Sunday in Lent, roughly midway through the fast.

clue.text: Manners of a man for all seasons

definitions.meaning: the customs and conventions of a society

definitions.text: of a man for all seasons
definitions.meaning: Sir Thomas More was the subject of the play A Man for All Seasons, so this means belonging to him

explanation.definitionFit: Social customs, from Latin; also More's, possessive of Thomas More, hero of Bolt's play.

clue.text: A way up in this, or down and out?

definitions.text: A way up in this, or down and out?

parts.words: A way up in this, or down and out?
parts.note: a burglar may climb a pipe to get up, and wasted things go 'down' one and out of the house

explanation.surface: A question about whether a route leads upwards or ends in ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down the' pipe means wasted; 'down and out' also means destitute.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe or channel carrying waste water away.

clue.text: Parts with the unhappy loser

indicators.note: an unhappy word is out of sorts, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gloomy defeated competitor takes leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors play parts, also called characters.

clue.text: Turn round if you want a fight. look

parts.note: a bout is a fight, especially a boxing match
face can mean look or expression

explanation.surface: A warning: turn around if you are looking for trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete reversal of direction or opinion, as in a military command to turn.

clue.text: What's the point in attacking?

parts.note: the sharp metal tip of a thrown weapon, and also the leading element of an assault

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question asking whether aggression is ever worthwhile.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointed tip of a lance, and figuratively the leader of an attack.

clue.text: Learn disorders of vital parts

indicators.note: the letters of the word are put out of order

explanation.surface: Learning about illnesses affecting the body's organs.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the kidneys, which are vital organs.
